title: Schedule list is not scoped to the authenticated user

evidence.quote: user_id: UUID | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="users.id", index=True)

reasoning: PodcastSchedule is modeled as user-owned, and authentication supports per-user credentials elsewhere, but this route only verifies that some credential is valid and then returns every schedule row. In a multi-user database, any valid user/API token can enumerate other users' schedule names, days, times, enabled state, and run history. The current test exercises only one authenticated user and only checks the list length, so it would not catch cross-user leakage.
reproduction: Create two users with separate API tokens and schedules assigned to different user_id values, then call GET /api/podcast/schedules using the second user's token. The response will include schedules for both users because the query has no user_id predicate.
recommendation: Resolve the authenticated user for schedule endpoints and filter the list query by that user_id. If legacy API_KEY/admin behavior is still required, make that path explicit instead of treating every valid credential as global access. Keep create/update/get/delete/trigger schedule ownership behavior consistent with the list route.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked schedule CRUD test uses a single auth_headers fixture and never creates schedules for two distinct users or asserts that another user's schedule is hidden.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates two users/API tokens, inserts or creates one PodcastSchedule per user, calls GET /api/podcast/schedules with each token, and asserts each response contains only that user's schedule.
minimumFixScope: GET /podcast/schedules query and the schedule CRUD ownership helper needed to derive the same authenticated user_id consistently.
